messages:
maria-ops: heads-up — after last night's image rebuilds that moved our base to CUDA 12/cuDNN 9, we started seeing cross-region failures. first noticed in us-west-2 autoscaled nodes.

daniel-infra: quick summary of symptoms?

maria-ops: short: containers built with CUDA 12 runtime are hitting runtime/driver mismatches on a subset of hosts. errors during startup: NCCL init failing, some runtimes crashing with `cudaErrorNoKernelImageForDevice` and `libcuda.so.1` version mismatch.

sasha-ml: do you have the actual error snippet?

maria-ops: paste below:
```
[2026-03-16 02:11:05] ERROR: NCCL: unhandled cudaErrorNoKernelImageForDevice
RuntimeError: CUDA error: no kernel image is available for execution on the device (cudaErrorNoKernelImageForDevice)
Caused by: /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so.12: undefined symbol: cuGetProcAddress
dlopen failed: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1: version `NVIDIA_DRIVER_535' required but `NVIDIA_DRIVER_525' found
```

zach-platform: that last line is the tell — host driver still at 525 on many nodes. images expect driver 535 which we didn't uniformly roll.

ops-oncall: infra-bot just auto-cordoned 4 nodes in us-west-2 due to repeated pod crashes :warning:

infra-bot: [k8s] node ip-10-0-7-21 cordoned (reason: pod crashloop from cuda runtime), pods evicted: 6

daniel-infra: how widespread? only us-west-2?

maria-ops: observed in us-west-2 and eu-central-1 so far. ap-southeast unaffected (still on older node pool with drivers pinned to 535). interestingly some GPU types (A10G) are more likely to fail vs A100 — probably kernel module ABI differences.

karen-devex: any build mistakes? did CI change the gcc used to compile kernels/ops in our images?

maria-ops: we rebuilt containers on Ubuntu 22.04 runners with GCC 12; older images used GCC 9. That changed libstdc++ and possibly PTX/cubin generation. Pointing to both host driver and compiled kernels mismatch.

sasha-ml: longer term fix is multi-arch multi-driver images, but short-term we need rollback/mitigation. suggestions?

daniel-infra: immediate plan I propose:
1) stop further CUDA12 image rollouts (CI gate) — already patched
2) add a shim tag `cuda12+host-535` only for nodes with driver >=535
3) schedule host driver upgrade for remaining nodes (maintenance window)
4) allow fallback to prior `cuda11` image for critical workloads

zach-platform: agree. also need to check node autoscaler: it spawned new nodes from an image that has older driver (525) but got the new container image, which caused mismatch. We should pin node pool images or change node labels so scheduler avoids mismatched images.

ops-oncall: rolling upgrade will impact capacity. if we cordon too many nodes we reduce GPU capacity and some jobs will queue — high-cost customers might be affected. we need communication to customers.

maria-ops: added a quick script to detect mismatch across nodes and list affected pods:
```
# run on master
for n in $(kubectl get nodes -l gpu=true -o name); do
  ssh $n "nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,gpu_name --format=csv" || echo $n failed
done
kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o wide | grep CrashLoopBackOff | grep -i cuda
```

sasha-ml: will create a canary image tag `cuda12-canary` which has runtime version check at container start and will exit with clear log if host driver < required. helps avoid silent crashes.

daniel-infra: operational steps for next 6 hours:
- pause CUDA12 image promotion (CI) — done
- label nodes: `kubectl label node <node> driver=525|535` based on nvidia-smi output
- update kube-scheduler predicate to avoid `cuda12` images on nodes without `driver=535` label (short-term mutate admission webhook)
- roll drivers in small batches with kernel module rebuild where needed (ops-oncall + zach)

ops-oncall: I'll start a maintenance page and ping top-tier customers. estimated capacity hit: 10-15% while we upgrade drivers in us-west.

zach-platform: note: driver upgrades require kernel module rebuild on nodes with custom kernels (on-prem/private). we need to coordinate with Private deployment team for air-gapped sites. may take longer.

karen-devex: I can draft a status blurb for the community forum and include mitigation steps for self-hosted customers.

maria-ops: temporary mitigations deployed:
- admission webhook rejecting cuda12 images on nodes without `driver=535`
- autoscaler paused for node pool `gpu-west-2-hot` to avoid new mismatched nodes
- created rollout ticket to upgrade drivers in 25-node batches starting 02:00 UTC

sasha-ml: add test matrix for CI: compile kernels with gcc9/11/12 and run integration on node driver 525/535 combos so we catch this earlier.

daniel-infra: longer-term: we should version images by minimum host driver and add runtime startup check to refuse to run when unsupported (fail fast and actionable logs). Also adopt multi-rootfs images orelse lightweight host runtime layer.

maria-ops: agreed. for now I'll monitor logs and report back in 2 hours. tagging @zach-platform @ops-oncall for rollout coordination.

ops-oncall: acknowledged. will maintain p0 channel and update when first batch complete.

zach-platform: small note — cost: rolling driver upgrades incur some extra on-demand GPU hours (~$3k/day if we keep capacity up). ops team please confirm budget ok.

daniel-infra: will open a cost approval for emergency O/T. thanks everyone.

maria-ops: status update 02:45 UTC — first 8 nodes upgraded to driver 535 + kubelet restart, no regressions observed. two jobs still failing due to leftover container GC; cleaning.

infra-bot: [alert] pods in ns=training show reduced retries after host driver upgrades; metrics stabilized.

maria-ops: thanks — will close out with postmortem doc and concrete CI changes. meeting in 30m to plan permanent guardrails.

karen-devex: saving notes for docs and examples for customers about how host driver vs container runtime interact. will post shortly.

(react emoji summary: :thumbsup: for actions, :eyes: monitoring)
